title: procurement-delegations-and-spot-purchase-playbook-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Title: Procurement delegations and spot‑purchase playbook (operational guidance)

Summary:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standard approach for low-latency procurement ("spot purchases"), sprint budget pools, and delegated approval thresholds. It defines who can approve purchases at each threshold, the required documentation for contracts and POs, expected SLAs for procurement execution, and the accounting/billing triggers relevant to revenue recognition and dedicated capacity billing. The objective is to enable product and engineering teams to move quickly while preserving controls required by Finance and Legal.

Scope:
- Applies to all product, infra, SRE, and ops teams requesting goods or services where the procurement value is less than or equal to $100,000 USD.
- Does NOT replace strategic sourcing for multi-year contracts, capital equipment (CAPEX > $100k), or transactions requiring legal review (see Exemptions).

Definitions:
- Spot purchase: One-off procurement for goods/services with single-payment or subscription <= 12 months and value <= approved threshold.
- Sprint budget pool: A pre-authorized aggregated budget assigned to an engineering squad for rapid purchases during a two-week sprint.
- Delegated authority: The explicit dollar limit a person or role may approve without additional approvals.
- Holdback clause: Procurement clause requiring vendor deliverable acceptance before invoicing milestone is recognized for revenue-impacting customers.

Delegation and approval matrix (effective):
| Tier | Max single purchase | Required documentation | Approver | Finance checklist | SLA (procurement ops) |
|------|--------------------:|-----------------------|---------|-------------------|-----------------------|
| A — Rapid (Sprint) | $2,500 | Short PO form + vendor W9 or equivalent | Squad lead | GL code + cost center | 24 hours |
| B — Team Delegate | $25,000 | Standard PO + vendor onboarding snapshot | Product manager / Team finance delegate | GL + budget pool tag | 48 hours |
| C — Department | $100,000 | PO + basic MSAs (if reuse expected) | Department head + Finance ops review | Budget owner signoff | 5 business days |

Exemptions (require Legal/Strategic Sourcing):
- Any purchase that:
  1) has data residency or IP transfer implications;
  2) includes indemnity/K holdback > standard;
  3) is multi-year > $100k total;
  4) modifies Redwood’s standard terms.
- For exemptions, raise a Legal intake ticket (legal-redwood) — do NOT use spot purchase bypass.

Procedure: Spot purchase (Tier A and B examples)
1) Confirm eligibility: purchaser confirms cost <= threshold and no data/IP implications.
2) Check sprint budget pool (if Tier A): verify available pool balance in ProcureFlow.
3) Vendor quick-check (required fields): vendor name, tax ID, banking method, address, basic risk flag (low/medium/high).
4) Complete minimal PO form in ProcureFlow: attach receipts/quotes and estimated GL code.
5) Approver signs digitally (Squad lead or PM role). For Tier B purchases, Finance ops receives auto-notification for review.
6) Procurement Ops issues PO within SLA. If vendor requires MSA, escalate to Legal within 48 hours.
7) After delivery, team confirms acceptance in ProcureFlow (acceptance date is used for invoice timing and any holdbacks).

Sprint budget pools (operational rules):
- Each engineering squad can request a sprint pool allocation (recommended default $7,500 per sprint) from Product Finance.
- Pool requests are submitted via the Sprint Budget request form two days before sprint start. Finance evaluates utilization history and grants or modifies the pool within 48 hours.
- Unused pool balances roll to the department pool at quarter end; they do not automatically carry forward to other departments.
- Large or repeat purchases that exceed 20% of a single sprint pool must be escalated to Department approval.

PO and invoice requirements (minimum):
- Merchant/vendor legal name
- Invoice with PO number, invoice date, payment terms
- Line-level description with SKU or brief scope
- GL code and cost center
- Delivery or acceptance confirmation where applicable
- For any vendor receiving >$25k annually, complete vendor risk questionnaire (VRQ) and store in Vendor Vault

Contract considerations for recurring/renewing spot-sourced services:
- If a spot purchase is renewed for the same vendor and the annualized spend is expected to exceed $25k, initiate a strategic sourcing intake 30 days before renewal.
- Avoid multi-term lock-ins for spot-purchased SaaS; prefer month-to-month or 90-day auto-renew with termination windows aligned to billing cycles.

Accounting & revenue recognition touchpoints:
- Invoice timing and revenue recognition: any customer-facing engineering work procured via spot purchase that is tied directly to an enterprise customer delivery (e.g., one-off feature or dedicated onboarding) must be tagged with the customer ID in ProcureFlow. Finance will assess whether costs are capitalizable or should be expensed immediately.
- PO acceptance date drives vendor invoice matching — accruals should be recorded in NetSuite the period the service is delivered/accepted.
- Holdback and milestone language: if vendor terms include an acceptance milestone linked to customer billing milestones, Legal and Finance must approve prior to issuance of PO. Exception handling requires a documented risk memo.

Billing and dedicated capacity interfaces:
- For purchases that support Dedicated or Private customer deployments (e.g., specialized infra installs), operations must flag the purchase as 'customer-impacting' in the PO. This ensures billing teams align usage/billing entitlements and prevents double-billing or missed pass-throughs.
- All cost pass-throughs must include a clear trace from PO -> internal cost center -> customer invoice line item. Finance Ops performs quarterly reconciliations.

Controls and monitoring:
- Finance Ops will run a weekly report showing all spot purchases, their tags (sprint-pool, customer-impacting, vendor-risk-level), and approvals. Any anomalies (e.g., split purchases to game thresholds) will trigger a procurement investigation.
- Random audit: 10% of Tier A purchases will be audited each quarter for policy compliance.

Escalations (common scenarios):
- Vendor requests expedited payment (< 7 days): Team lead and Finance ops must approve; mark as ‘urgent’ in ProcureFlow with reason.
- Unavailable PO accommodate: If vendor refuses to accept Redwood PO, Procurement Ops must document the exception, obtain the Department head signoff, and route to Legal if the vendor requires alternate terms.

Runbook: Typical Tier B purchase (example)
1) Developer raises request in Jira ticket with cost estimate and link to vendor quote.
2) PM buys from sprint pool or submits PO request.
3) Team finance delegate approves and adds GL/cost center.
4) Procurement Ops issues PO and vendors are onboarded (if new).
5) Delivery, acceptance, invoice submission, and NetSuite booking.

Owner and responsibilities:
- Procurement Ops (owner): maintain ProcureFlow templates, run SLA dashboards, perform weekly spot purchase reporting.
- Finance Ops: validate GL coding, run reconciliations, audit spot purchases.
- Legal: review any contract with nonstandard terms or data/IP clauses.
- Squad leads and PMs: ensure requests comply with sprint pool rules and capture acceptance evidence.

Metrics and targets:
- PO issuance SLA: Tier A — 24h, Tier B — 48h, Tier C — 5 business days.
- Compliance target: 95% of spot purchases completed with a valid PO and acceptance evidence.
- Audit pass rate: > 90% of audited Tier A purchases meet policy requirements.

Appendix A — Example PO JSON snippet (for ProcureFlow API):
{
  "po_number": "PO-2026-4321",
  "vendor": "Acme Cloud Tools LLC",
  "amount": "1850.00",
  "currency": "USD",
  "cost_center": "ENG-SQUAD-17",
  "line_items": ["SaaS seat: 10 x monthly"],
  "tags": ["sprint-pool", "tier-a"]
}

Appendix B — Quick checklist for approvers:
- Is this within my delegated authority?
- Has vendor been screened for sanctions and basic risk?
- Is there a customer or revenue recognition implication? If yes, flag to Finance.
- Do I see a valid GL and cost center?
